_note: Optional tension library. Key: alphabetically sorted primary-index pair joined by '__'. Each value contains copy for a real square or opposition between active driver bodies. Do not render from this library merely because two indexes are present.
fallback: Two active patterns are asking for coordination. The tension is not a verdict; it identifies where one useful capacity can become costly when it acts without awareness of the other. Name the competing needs, then choose a practical adjustment that gives both a place in the next decision.

catalyst__dfis.square: Catalyst pressure can activate a depth response before you have fully named what is being protected. Change may feel urgent, while old anger, desire, or self-protection asks for recognition. Do not let speed choose for you. Identify the boundary beneath the reaction, then make the change that restores agency rather than merely releasing pressure.
catalyst__dfis.opposition: A disruption outside you may reflect an inner conflict around autonomy, vulnerability, or power. The task is not to force a break or retreat into control. Let the external shift show where a deeper need has been waiting for a more conscious form. Clear terms turn intensity into a usable decision.

catalyst__kvq.square: The urge to act can collide with an early perception that something is not yet fully clear. You may feel pushed to move before the pattern has enough evidence, or tempted to delay action until certainty arrives. Use the tension as a timing tool: test the signal, then choose the smallest move that creates real information.
catalyst__kvq.opposition: An external turning point may challenge what you thought you saw coming. Let the surprise refine foresight rather than discredit it. A useful response balances alertness with flexibility, allowing new evidence to alter the plan without requiring you to abandon your own discernment.

catalyst__mki.square: A change impulse may conflict with loyalty to memory, lineage, or an established way of making meaning. The pressure can make the past feel either sacred or burdensome. Neither extreme is required. Ask what deserves continuity, what needs repair, and what must be allowed to end so the story can continue honestly.
catalyst__mki.opposition: External change may bring an inherited pattern into view. A person, event, or opportunity can show where old knowledge still has value and where it is preventing movement. Treat memory as counsel, not command. The next step becomes clearer when you separate preservation from repetition.

catalyst__nge.square: The story you thought you were living may be interrupted by a change that refuses to fit its expected plot. Resist the urge to force the disruption into a familiar role too quickly. The tension asks for authorship: decide which part of the narrative has truly changed and what new action the revised story now makes possible.
catalyst__nge.opposition: A turning point may arrive through a person or circumstance that carries a different story-world than the one you have been inhabiting. Let the contrast widen the narrative rather than turn it into a battle for the correct plot. A new genre may be asking for a new strategy.

catalyst__rwi.square: A system-level pattern may need revision faster than the available structure can comfortably absorb. Change can expose how many practical details have been held together by habit alone. Avoid dramatic overhaul for its own sake. Map the pressure point, alter one condition, and let the redesign prove itself through use.
catalyst__rwi.opposition: Outside disruption can reveal a structural truth you had not yet acted on. The task is to treat the event as data rather than a command to react. Notice what the interruption made visible, then build a response that improves the system instead of merely surviving the moment.

dfis__kvq.square: Deep feeling and early perception may become entangled, making it hard to tell whether a warning comes from present reality, old injury, or both. Do not dismiss the signal, but do not hand it total authority. Ground the insight in observable facts and name the boundary that would protect you either way.
dfis__kvq.opposition: Another person's response may mirror a private tension between wanting to be believed and needing to remain self-possessed. You do not have to prove your perception through intensity. State what you see, clarify what you need, and let evidence carry the part that emotion cannot settle alone.

dfis__mki.square: Memory can activate a depth response before the present situation has been fully evaluated. Old loyalties, grief, or survival knowledge may be real, yet they can make a current choice feel more loaded than it is. Slow down enough to distinguish inheritance from immediacy, then choose the boundary that serves the life you have now.
dfis__mki.opposition: A present encounter may draw a line between what you remember and what you are no longer willing to carry. Let the contrast clarify rather than shame you. You can honor the origin of a pattern while refusing to let it determine the terms of your next relationship, decision, or obligation.

dfis__nge.square: A powerful inner truth may clash with the story-role you have been expected to play. You may feel pressure to remain the healer, villain, survivor, rescuer, or loyal one even as a deeper part of you refuses the script. The work is to revise the role without denying the feeling that made it necessary.
dfis__nge.opposition: A person or circumstance may reflect a narrative that intensifies desire, anger, grief, or self-protection. Do not let the dramatic charge decide the meaning. Name the real need beneath the scene, then choose an action that protects your agency without requiring you to become smaller or harder than you are.

dfis__rwi.square: A practical pattern may be asking for change while a deeper attachment makes the old arrangement difficult to release. You may understand the system clearly and still feel pulled by desire, loyalty, fear, or history. Treat that conflict with respect. Structural change lasts when the emotional cost has also been named and supported.
dfis__rwi.opposition: An external system, rule, or relationship dynamic may expose where your private boundaries have been doing too much work alone. Let the contrast reveal which condition needs redesign, documentation, or redistribution. You do not have to solve a structural problem by becoming endlessly resilient.

kvq__mki.square: Foresight and memory may disagree about what the future requires. One part of you recognizes an emerging pattern, while another remains loyal to what has been learned, promised, or survived before. Let both speak. The useful question is which lesson from the past helps you meet the future without recreating it.
kvq__mki.opposition: A current signal may arrive through someone or something that challenges the story you have carried from the past. Listen for the difference between revision and betrayal. You can let new evidence reshape an inherited conclusion while still honoring the experience that made the old conclusion necessary.

kvq__nge.square: You may see where a story is heading before you know how to inhabit the present chapter without forcing it. The tension can produce urgency, fatalism, or a wish to skip the difficult middle. Keep the future in view, but make the next decision from what is true now. Foresight works best when it leaves room for authorship.
kvq__nge.opposition: Another person or event may offer a competing story about what the pattern means. Treat the contrast as a chance to refine your reading rather than defend it reflexively. A future-facing insight becomes more useful when it can hold multiple possible paths and still guide one clear next step.

kvq__rwi.square: An early intuitive read may be ahead of the available structure, evidence, or language needed to communicate it. The frustration is understandable, but the solution is translation. Gather the details, make the pattern legible, and let your perception become a practical warning, proposal, or boundary rather than a private burden.
kvq__rwi.opposition: External facts may challenge the first interpretation you made of an emerging pattern. Let correction strengthen the signal instead of making you distrust yourself. The aim is not to be right at the earliest possible moment; it is to become more accurate, more useful, and better able to act when the pattern matters.

mki__nge.square: The story you inherited may not match the story you are becoming. Memory, family mythology, or prior identity can pull toward continuity while the present genre asks for a different role. Do not frame this as disloyalty by default. Choose which threads belong in the future and which ones have completed their work.
mki__nge.opposition: A person or circumstance may invite you into a story that feels unfamiliar because it departs from what you were taught to expect. Let the difference reveal what you value, not just what you fear losing. A new narrative can honor the past without preserving every limitation it contained.

mki__rwi.square: What you remember and what the system currently requires may be pulling in different directions. An old method, loyalty, or explanation can make it harder to see the present structure clearly. Use the tension to update the archive: preserve the lesson, but let the operational reality guide the next decision.
mki__rwi.opposition: An external arrangement may show where memory has been carrying information that needs a new container. Records, routines, agreements, or boundaries can help translate experience into something usable. The goal is not to reduce the past to data, but to keep its wisdom from being lost to repetition or confusion.

nge__rwi.square: The story you want to live may be ahead of the conditions currently supporting it. This can feel like a clash between imagination and practicality, but it is better understood as a design problem. Identify the missing structure, resource, or agreement that would let the desired narrative become more than a hope.
nge__rwi.opposition: A real-world condition may challenge the story you have been telling yourself about what should happen next. Let the fact revise the plot without collapsing the meaning. A narrative becomes stronger when it can adapt to reality and still preserve the values that made it worth pursuing.
